sources: Patterns re-implemented from Mole (tw93/Mole, lib/clean) and Kudu (AdventDevInc/kudu, rules/darwin and rules/win32, MIT). No code copied. Windows rules (platforms: windows) re-implement the same categories for per-user folders only; Delivery Optimization and Windows Update caches need administrator rights and are deliberately not covered. Pack 2 adds 276 rules ported from Kudu's rule data (AdventDevInc/kudu, MIT: see NOTICE), reviewed per bogusyogi/rightkit#1530.

rules.reason: Temporary copies of the Chrome app that a killed Chrome left behind. They are clones that share storage with the real app, so the size you get back is far smaller than the size shown.

rules.name: Installers
rules.reason: An installer you have probably used already. Some .exe files are portable programs you run from here, so look first; one that is running is skipped.

rules.name: Old downloads
rules.reason: Not modified in over 90 days. These are your own files, so look before you move them.

rules.name: Crash dumps
rules.reason: Memory dumps from crashed programs, often large. Keep one if you are chasing that crash.

rules.name: Windows error reports
rules.reason: Crash reports Windows saved for you; nothing needs them once you have looked.

rules.name: Thumbnail and icon cache
rules.reason: Explorer rebuilds these previews on demand. Explorer keeps them open, so they are offered only when it is not running.

rules.name: Electron app caches
rules.reason: Cached web content and compiled code of VS Code, Slack, Discord and Teams; each app rebuilds it. Not touched while the app is running. Never your sign-in, settings or messages.

rules.name: Browser on-device models
rules.reason: AI model files the browser downloaded for on-device features, often several gigabytes. The browser downloads them again if it needs them, which uses your connection.

rules.name: Browser crash reports
rules.reason: Crash dumps the browser saved to send to its maker; nothing needs them once you have looked.

rules.name: iOS simulators
rules.reason: Old simulators take space. Remove unused ones in Terminal with: xcrun simctl delete unavailable

rules.name: Trash
